subject: history_social
passage: Machu Picchu sits on a narrow ridge high above the Urubamba River in the Andes of Peru. Built around 1450, probably as a royal estate for the Inca ruler Pachacuti, and abandoned roughly a century later, ______ Many of its walls were made of granite blocks cut so precisely that they fit together without mortar.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the site was never discovered by the Spanish conquistadors, so many of its buildings remain largely intact.
choices.B: the Spanish conquistadors never discovered the site, so many of its buildings remain largely intact.
choices.C: historians note that the site was never discovered by the Spanish conquistadors, so many of its buildings remain largely intact.
choices.D: the Spanish conquistadors' failure to discover the site explains why many of its buildings remain largely intact.

explanation.why: The introductory modifier "Built around 1450 ... and abandoned roughly a century later" describes the place as a whole: Machu Picchu was the royal estate that was built and abandoned. The noun right after the comma must therefore be "the site." Choice D is the near miss: it begins with "the Spanish conquistadors' failure," but the subject is "failure," not the site.
explanation.A: Correct. "The site" comes right after the modifier, so it is the site that was built as a royal estate and later abandoned.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Placing "the Spanish conquistadors" right after the modifier says the conquistadors were built as a royal estate, so the modifier dangles.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Placing "historians" right after the modifier says the historians were built around 1450 and abandoned, which makes no sense.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The subject is "failure" ("conquistadors' " is only a possessive), so the sentence says a failure was built as a royal estate and later abandoned.
